Alex — great questions, answering inline below and added a short proposal for the infra sync.

1) Bursts vs steady-state (embeddings):
  - Short bursts (up to ~3 minutes) are best handled by enabling a small burst buffer on the Dedicated pool + short-lived autoscaling policy that allows +25% headroom for bursts. For your pattern (avg 10k/min, peaks 18k/min), we recommend baseline capacity sized for 12k/min sustained with autoscale headroom to cover the 18k/min spikes. That keeps steady-state costs reasonable while covering short bursts.

2) Concurrency for chat:
  - With our profiling for models like redwood-large/quantized variants, target per-GPU concurrency of 24–32 concurrent requests for interactive chat when median prompt lengths are ~220 tokens. This assumes batching is limited to 50–100ms to preserve latency SLOs. For tail latency, we recommend a small request queue per worker (queue depth 64) plus a fast-path routing policy to avoid head-of-line blocking.

3) KMS/mTLS:
  - Customer-managed KMS is supported for Dedicated today (we integrate with major cloud KMS providers). mTLS is also supported on Dedicated — we'll share our certificate rotation guidance in the infra sync.

Infra sync proposal: Wed 9/16 10:00am PT — Marissa (solutions), Aditya (RT infra), Dev (runtime/ops) + FinTechX infra/security. We'll use the Drive link I shared for artifacts.

Attaching an updated MAP that adds the sizing baseline and a short table of recommended autoscale thresholds.

Team — forwarding the thread and adding a few technical items to prepare for the infra sync. Internal-only notes: 

• For embeddings baseline: assume each embedding request (model: embed-small-v1, quantized) costs ~0.008 GPU-seconds per item when batched at 512 examples. At 12k/min that's ~96k embeddings/hour -> ~768 GPU-seconds/hour -> ~0.213 GPU-hours -> per-hour pool sizing is modest but spikes matter. Recommend we show FinTechX a projection for: baseline (12k/min), peak burst (18k/min), and extreme (25k/min) with corresponding GPU counts and cost delta.

• Queueing: use a front-door queue (per-region) with token-aware batching; keep per-worker concurrency limit at 32 to meet chat latency targets. Backpressure policy: reject bursts that exceed autoscale headroom with a clear 429 + retry-after semantics.

• Auth/KMS: collect FinTechX KMS provider and key policy during the infra sync — we'll confirm if any cross-account IAM steps are needed.

Can someone (Dev) draft the sizing table and brief projection slide (1 slide) before EOD today so we can include in the sync deck?

Alex / Aditya / Marissa — jumping in with the sizing slide and some concrete recommendations ahead of the sync. See summary below and I'll bring the deck to the call: 

Sizing summary (recommendation):
• Embeddings (batch): baseline pool = 6 x g4-equivalent GPUs -> supports ~12k embeddings/min with 512 batching and 80% packing efficiency.
• Burst coverage: allow autoscale to +50% (up to 9 GPUs) with scale-up cooldown 60s and scale-down cooldown 300s. This covers 18k/min bursts while avoiding flapping.
• Chat (interactive): 2 x g4-equivalent GPUs dedicated for chat VMs with per-GPU concurrency target = 28, per-worker queue depth = 64, and max overall queue per-region = 200. Use latency-first routing for chat traffic.
• Concurrency limits: per-request timeout = 20s, hard concurrency cap per-GPU = 32, soft cap = 28.
• Backpressure behavior: on queue depth > 75% mark, return 429 + Retry-After to clients and route to a degraded model variant if configured.

Operational notes:
• Monitoring: we'll provide per-route latency and queue-length dashboards; plan an alert when autoscale spend reaches 80% of commit.
• Security: Dev keys for test can be created via our Console; for production we'll enable customer KMS integration (we need their key ARN).

I'll attach the one-slide sizing deck to the calendar invite and drop the recommended autoscale thresholds into the MAP spreadsheet. See you on the 16th.
